method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; a seat-neutral core (limitation-core.l4: dates with built-in date functions only, the choice of regime, discoverability, legal incapacity, the Part IIA periods, extension, Division 5's earlier judgments and settlements, Part I with Part II) and one seat layer that restates no rule (limitation-seat.l4, 15 questions with @export and @desc); one regulative rule (the bar: the plaintiff DO bring the action WITHIN the days to the last day, LEST BREACH meaning barred), tested by EVALTRACE, never taken as an input; no REFUSE (a case outside the encoding answers NOTHING, asserted); checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Limitation of Actions Act 1958 (Vic), Act No. 6295/1958, Version No. 113 as at 2 October 2026 (including s 23AB and the s 40 amendment, No. 45/2026 ss 18E, 18F, in force 2 October 2026, and the Division 5 amendments of No. 5/2026 ss 4-9, in force 25 February 2026), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/limitation-of-actions-act-1958.txt (sha256 84e874841a2b4d3ad2348a1304bd7b36be7b23607bfb485db8d2ab886eb689bd), converted from the Word file the owner saved by hand on 2026-11-07

seat: the injured person (or, after a death, the executor or administrator bringing a survivor action, or the dependants bringing a Wrongs Act Part III action; for Division 5, the person abused as a child) asking whether, and until when, they can still sue

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run limitation-core.l4 ; l4 run limitation-seat.l4 ; l4 run limitation-cases.l4
checks.result: 120 written, 120 satisfied in limitation-cases.l4; 0 errors, 0 warnings in all three files (2026-11-07)
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read; a copy of the case file with two expected values changed was run outside the repository to confirm failures are reported (2 failed), and not kept.

scope: In: s 3(2), (3); s 4; s 5(1)(a), (1AA), (1A), (9); s 23(1) with proviso (a), (1A); s 23A(2), (4), (6); s 23AB; s 27(1); Part IIA Division 1 (ss 27A, 27B), Division 2 (ss 27C-27J), Division 3 (ss 27K, 27L as factors, 27M), Division 4 (s 27N except (3)), Division 5 (ss 27O, 27OA, 27P, 27Q, 27QA-27QF, 27R(2), (3), 27T); s 33 and s 40 as the reasons a case is outside. Inputs: the dates a fact was or ought to have been known, the court's judgments (just and reasonable, length of extension), close associate, the borrowed terms (dust-related condition, survivor action, Part III action, represented person, the schemes, National Redress Scheme). Out: defamation (ss 5(1AAA)-(1AAD), 5A, 5B, 23B-23D), the other Part I heads (s 5(1)(b)-(d), (2)-(8), ss 6-22), s 23(1) provisos (b)-(d), s 23(2), s 23A(3), ss 24-26, s 27 proviso and (2), s 27N(3), s 27R(1), s 27S, ss 1, 2, 28-41 other than ss 33 and 40, and the earlier law kept by ss 27N(4) and 40 (not deposited). See NOTES.md.
